meta.title: Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant.
items.comment: There is no need to transpose this provision into national legislation.

items.text: 2. The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall apply to persons from the time that they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether they have committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

provisions.comment: In Croatian criminal justice legislation, an accused person is normally instructed through a letter of rights. The letter of rights is delivered to the suspect or the accused person with some other procedural decisions which take place in the early stages of the proceedings.
provisions.textEn:
(2) The notification of rights shall be served on the defendant together with:

1) the search warrant;

2) the summons to the first interrogation;

3) the investigation order;

4) the summons to the evidentiary hearing;

5) the notice referred to in Article 213, paragraph 2, of the present Act;

6) the investigative imprisonment order;

7) the identification warrant;

8) the warrant for the examination of the person of the defendant by an expert witness.

If an act within the proceedings is not being taken in the language which the person speaks and understands, oral translation or sign language translation and interpretation for the deaf and the deaf and blind of what this person or another person is saying and of the documents and any other written evidentiary material being adduced shall be provided. 

﻿The person shall be instructed of his right to oral translation or sign language translation or interpretation for the deaf and the deaf and blind before his first examination.

2) use in the proceedings his native language or the language spoken and understood by him, including the sign language of the deaf and the deaf and blind and if he does not understand the Croatian language, the right to an interpreter or translator or if he is deaf or deaf and blind, a sign language interpreter;

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (4) The defendant within the meaning of Article 202, paragraph 3, of this Act who neither speaks nor understands the language of the proceedings or who is deaf or mute or deaf and blind shall be entitled to translation.

(5) A written translation of the notification of rights, the decision on the deprivation of liberty, the investigation order and the order for the taking of evidentiary actions, the indictment, the private charge, the summons, the court decision following the filing of the charges until the conclusion of the proceedings by a final judgment and in proceedings on extraordinary remedies shall be provided to the defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article.

items.comment: In Croatian criminal justice system, person against whom law enforcement authorities are undertaking actions and measures in order to resolve the suspicion that he/she has committed a criminal offence, enjoys all the basic rights of the defence in criminal proceedings, including the right to interpretation and translation. Therefore, a suspect is informed about the charge and his/her rights very early in the proceedings, at the time of his/her first contact with the police or other law enforcement authority in the capacity of a suspect (when summoned to be interrogated by the police, when arrested, and together with some other decisions on procedurally important actions). A suspect or an accused person enjoys all his/her basic rights of the defence, including the right to interpretation and translation until the conclusion of the proceedings (final determination of the question whether the suspect or the accused person has committed the criminal offence).

items.text: 3. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court following such an appeal.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Prekršajnog zakona (13)
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Misdemeanor Act

provisions.textEn: 2) Parties to the proceedings, witnesses and other persons participating in the proceedings shall have the right to use their own language. If the proceedings or individual actions in the proceedings are not conducted in the language of that person, an oral translation of what they or others present and the document and other written evidence will be provided. If the person does not understand the language of the proceedings, translation will be provided in each case. Translation is done by the interpreter.

items.comment: The Directive applies not only to the proceedings before the courts, but also to the first instance misdemeanour proceedings conducted by the administrative bodies (for example the tax authorities or customs).

items.text: 4. This Directive does not affect national law concerning the presence of legal counsel during any stage of the criminal proceedings, nor does it affect national law concerning the right of access of a suspected or accused person to documents in criminal proceedings.
items.comment: In Criminal Procedure Act there are no provisions in this regard, but it is implied.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not speak or understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are provided, without delay, with interpretation during criminal proceedings before investigative and judicial authorities, including during police questioning, all court hearings and any necessary interim hearings.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(2))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (3) The parties and other participants in the proceedings are entitled to use their native language. If a particular act within the framework of the proceedings is not conducted in the language which the person speaks and understands, oral translation of what this person or other persons are saying and of the documents and other written evidentiary materials being presented shall be provided. It shall be noted in the protocol that the instruction and statements by participants have been given. The person shall be instructed of his right to oral translation before the first interrogation.

(1) Under the present Act the defendant shall have the right to:

2) use in the proceedings his native language or the language spoken and understood by him, including the sign language of the deaf and the deaf and blind and if he does not understand the Croatian language, the right to an interpreter or translator or if he is deaf or deaf and blind, a sign language interpreter;

nationalActs.title: Zakon o kaznenom postupku
nationalActs.titleEn: Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (1) Where this Act so provides, the interrogation of the defendant shall be conducted through an interpreter.

items.comment: Criminal Procedure Act provides the right to interpretation in Article 8 and it is listed as an rights of the defendant in Article 64(1). The Article 280(1) stipulates that the interrogation should be conducted through interpreted where the Act so provides. The suspect or the accused person is informed of the right to interpretation when summoned by the police as a suspect (Article 208a par 2), arrested (108a par 4) and in the letter of rights (Article 239 par 1).

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that, where necessary for the purpose of safeguarding the fairness of the proceedings, interpretation is available for communication between suspected or accused persons and their legal counsel in direct connection with any questioning or hearing during the proceedings or with the lodging of an appeal or other procedural applications.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(2))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (8) The defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article is also entitled to the translation of the conversations and the correspondence with his defence counsel that are required for preparing the defence, filing legal relief or a legal remedy or taking other actions within the framework of the proceedings where this is necessary for the exercise of procedural defence rights. Translation shall be provided at the request of the defendant.

items.text: 3. The right to interpretation under paragraphs 1 and 2 includes appropriate assistance for persons with hearing or speech impediments.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o kaznenom postupku
nationalActs.titleEn: Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (2) If the defendant is deaf, questions shall be posed to him in writing, and if he is mute, he shall be invited to answer questions in writing. If the interrogation cannot be performed in this manner, a person who is able to communicate with the defendant shall be called upon to act as an interpreter.

nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (3) The parties to and other participants in the proceedings shall be entitled to use their native language, including the sign language of the deaf and the deaf and blind. If an act within the proceedings is not being taken in the language which the person speaks and understands, oral translation or sign language translation and interpretation for the deaf and the deaf and blind of what this person or another person is saying and of the documents and any other written evidentiary material being adduced shall be provided. It shall be noted in the minutes that the notification was read and statements by the participants given. The person shall be instructed of his right to oral translation or sign language translation or interpretation for the deaf and the deaf and blind before his first examination.

(1) Under the present Act the defendant shall have the right to:

2) use in the proceedings his native language or the language spoken and understood by him, including the sign language of the deaf and the deaf and blind and if he does not understand the Croatian language, the right to an interpreter or translator or if he is deaf or deaf and blind, a sign language interpreter;

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that a procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o kaznenom postupku
nationalActs.titleEn: Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (1) When being interrogated for the first time, the defendant shall be asked to state his full name, his aliases, if he has any, the full names of his parents, his mother’s maiden name, place of birth, home address, date of birth, ethnicity, nationality, occupation, profession, employment and educational background, personal identification number, family situation, military rank, if he has one, decorations, if he has been decorated, financial situation, previous convictions and, if any, when and for what, sentences served and, if he has served any, when, ongoing criminal proceedings against him for some other offence, if any, and, if he is a minor, the name of his legal representative.

(6) If there is doubt as to whether the defendant understands the official language of the court or if circumstances referred to in Article 280 of this Act exist, the defendant shall be instructed that the interrogation shall be conducted through an interpreter. The authority conducting the interrogation shall ensure the participation of the interpreter prior to the interrogation.

items.comment: There is no specific procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter. It is only partially implemented through the provisions on the obligatory questions about the ethnicity and nationality of the defendant when he/she is interrogated for the first time and the obligation to use interpreter in a case of doubt whether the defendant understands the official language of the court.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation and, when interpretation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the interpretation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

(1) A substantive violation of the provisions of criminal procedure exists in the following cases: 

...

3) if the trial was held in the absence of a person whose presence at the trial is mandatory under law or if the accused, defence counsel, subsidiary prosecutor or private prosecutor was, contrary to his request, denied the right to use his language at the trial and to follow trial proceedings in his language (Article 8);

(3) A substantive violation of the provisions of criminal procedure also exists if the court, in preparing or in the course of the trial or in rendering the judgment, fails to apply or incorrectly applies any of the provisions of this Act or violates a right of the defence at the trial, provided that this influenced or could have influenced the rendering of the judgment.

(1) Unless the appeal is explicitly barred by this Act, the parties and persons whose rights have been violated may file an appeal against an order of the State Attorney or the judge of investigation as well as against other orders of the court of first instance.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(2))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn:
(1) Any defendant who after the service of the investigation order deems that contrary to law he has been denied a right or that any one of his rights has been violated may file a written complaint with the State Attorney. The complaint cannot be filed for any of the reasons for which an appeal against the investigation order may be filed.

(2) After service of the notice referred to in Article 213, paragraph 2, of the present Act, the defendant may file a written complaint with the State Attorney for either of the reasons referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article or if he deems that the statutory conditions for the taking of the fact-finding activity are not fulfilled.

items.comment: The Art 8 CPA provides only for the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for translation or that the quality of translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings. During investigation, or simplified investigation the defendant can file a written complaint for the protection of procedural defence rights to the State Attorney against the decision that there is no need for interpretation or against the non-sufficient quality of the interpretation. To challenge the decision on interpretation is possible in the appellate procedure, where the denial of the defendant's right to use his/her language is listed as one of the substantive violations of the provisions of criminal procedure.

items.text: 6. Where appropriate, communication technology such as videoconferencing, telephone or the Internet may be used, unless the physical presence of the interpreter is required in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

items.comment: The use of internet is not mentioned in the implementing provision, but it is covered by the translation and interpretation "via audio-video device".

items.text: 7. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide persons subject to such proceedings who do not speak or understand the language of the proceedings with interpretation in accordance with this Article.

nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Act on Judicial Cooperation in Criminal Matters with the Member States of the European Union

provisions.textEn: (1) Immediately after the arrest of a person requested for the purpose of executing a European arrest warrant, the police shall instruct that person in writing about the rights of the arrested person exercising in accordance with the provisions of domestic criminal procedural law.

(2) Prior to the examination, the State Attorney shall instruct the requested person about his rights which he exercises in accordance with the provisions of domestic criminal procedural law:

- the right to interpretation and translation,

items.text: 8. Interpretation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o kaznenom postupku
nationalActs.titleEn: Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn:
(1) Where this Act so provides, the interrogation of the defendant shall be conducted through an interpreter. 

(2) If the defendant is deaf, questions shall be posed to him in writing, and if he is mute, he shall be invited to answer questions in writing. If the interrogation cannot be performed in this manner, a person who is able to communicate with the defendant shall be called upon to act as an interpreter. 

(3) If the interpreter has not previously taken an oath, he shall take an oath that he will faithfully communicate questions put to the defendant as well as statements given by the defendant. 

(4) The provisions of this Act that apply to expert witnesses shall accordingly apply to interpreters.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (11) The translation and interpretation shall be provided by an interpreter.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o sudovima
nationalActs.titleEn: Judiciary Act

provisions.textEn: At the request of a court, state body, legal entity or citizen, permanent court interpreters translate spoken or written text from Croatian into a foreign language, from a foreign language into Croatian or from a foreign language into another foreign language.

(1) A person who has completed a graduate university degree, is fluent in an appropriate foreign language and a language in official use and has a satisfactory level of general and legal knowledge may be appointed as a permanent court interpreter.

(2) Permanent court interpreters shall be appointed and dismissed by the president of the county court. Permanent court interpreters are appointed for a term of four years, after which they may be reappointed. Appointed permanent court interpreters may provide translation services throughout the Republic of Croatia.

(4) The Minister of Justice shall prescribe by an ordinance the conditions and procedure for the appointment of permanent court interpreters, their rights and duties, as well as the amount of remuneration and reimbursement of expenses for their work.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: Right to translation of essential documents

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are, within a reasonable period of time, provided with a written translation of all documents which are essential to ensure that they are able to exercise their right of defence and to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (4) The defendant within the meaning of Article 202, paragraph 3, of this Act who neither speaks nor understands the language of the proceedings or who is deaf or mute or deaf and blind shall be entitled to translation.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(2))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (5) A written translation of the notification of rights, the decision on the deprivation of liberty, the investigation order and the order for the taking of evidentiary actions, the indictment, the private charge, the summons, the court decision following the filing of the charges until the conclusion of the proceedings by a final judgment and in proceedings on extraordinary remedies shall be provided to the defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article. If the said documents are not available in the language which the defendant speaks and understands, they shall be translated to the defendant orally and a written translation thereof into the language spoken and understood by the defendant shall be provided to the defendant in the shortest possible time. If the defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article cannot read the said documents, they shall be presented to him in a way which he understands.

items.text: 2. Essential documents shall include any decision depriving a person of his liberty, any charge or indictment, and any judgment.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(2))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (5) A written translation of the notification of rights, the decision on the deprivation of liberty, the investigation order and the order for the taking of evidentiary actions, the indictment, the private charge, the summons, the court decision following the filing of the charges until the conclusion of the proceedings by a final judgment and in proceedings on extraordinary remedies shall be provided to the defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article.

items.text: 3. The competent authorities shall, in any given case, decide whether any other document is essential. Suspected or accused persons or their legal counsel may submit a reasoned request to that effect.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: 6) The body conducting the proceedings may of its own motion or upon a reasoned written request of the defendant order that a written translation of a piece of evidence or a part thereof be provided where this is necessary for the exercise of procedural defence rights.

items.text: 4. There shall be no requirement to translate passages of essential documents which are not relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.comment: The Art 8(6) CPA mentions only "evidence”, so the other essential documents must therefore be translated in full. The phrase "necessary for the exercise of procedural defence rights" includes the passages "relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them." It can be concluded that the Croatian law sets the higher standards in this regard.
provisions.textEn: 6) The body conducting the proceedings may of its own motion or upon a reasoned written request of the defendant order that a written translation of a piece of evidence or a part thereof be provided where this is necessary for the exercise of procedural defence rights.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for the translation of documents or passages thereof and, when a translation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

items.text: 6. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide any person subject to such proceedings who does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State, with a written translation of that document.

(2) Prior to the examination, the State Attorney shall instruct the requested person about his rights which he exercises in accordance with the provisions of domestic criminal procedural law:

- the right to interpretation and translation,

provisions.textEn: (5) A written translation of the notification of rights, the decision on the deprivation of liberty, the investigation order and the order for the taking of evidentiary actions, the indictment, the private charge, the summons, the court decision following the filing of the charges until the conclusion of the proceedings by a final judgment and in proceedings on extraordinary remedies shall be provided to the defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article.

items.comment: Act on Judicial Cooperation in Criminal Matters with the Member States of the European Union does not explicitly provide for a written translation of a European arrest warrant if the requested person does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State. Art. 24(3) AJCCM provides only that the state attorney has to inform the requested person about the content and basis for issuing a European arrest warrant. However, Art 24(1) AJCCM provides that the police have to inform the person upon arrest about the rights provided in accordance with the rules of domestic criminal procedure. Even though EAW is not explicitly mentioned as an essential document in Art. 8(5) CPA, it is a decision on the deprivation of liberty that has to be translated.

items.text: 7. As an exception to the general rules established in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6, an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents may be provided instead of a written translation on condition that such oral translation or oral summary does not prejudice the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: Exceptionally, an oral translation or oral summary of evidence may be provided instead of a written translation on condition that procedural defence rights are not violated thereby and that the defendant has a defence counsel.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(2))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: If the said documents are not available in the language which the defendant speaks and understands, they shall be translated to the defendant orally and a written translation thereof into the language spoken and understood by the defendant shall be provided to the defendant in the shortest possible time.

items.text: 8. Any waiver of the right to translation of documents referred to in this Article shall be subject to the requirements that suspected or accused persons have received prior legal advice or have otherwise obtained full knowledge of the consequences of such a waiver, and that the waiver was unequivocal and given voluntarily.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (7) The defendant referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article may waive his right to written translation after he has been instructed of the consequences of such waiver by the body conducting the proceedings. The waiver must be made freely and unambiguously and must be signed by the defendant.

items.text: 9. Translation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o sudovima
nationalActs.titleEn: Judiciary Act

provisions.textEn: At the request of a court, state body, legal entity or citizen, permanent court interpreters translate spoken or written text from Croatian into a foreign language, from a foreign language into Croatian or from a foreign language into another foreign language.

(1) A person who has completed a graduate university degree, is fluent in an appropriate foreign language and a language in official use and has a satisfactory level of general and legal knowledge may be appointed as a permanent court interpreter.

(2) Permanent court interpreters shall be appointed and dismissed by the president of the county court. Permanent court interpreters are appointed for a term of four years, after which they may be reappointed. Appointed permanent court interpreters may provide translation services throughout the Republic of Croatia.

(4) The Minister of Justice shall prescribe by an ordinance the conditions and procedure for the appointment of permanent court interpreters, their rights and duties, as well as the amount of remuneration and reimbursement of expenses for their work.

items.text: Member States shall meet the costs of interpretation and translation resulting from the application of Articles 2 and 3, irrespective of the outcome of the proceedings.
items.heading: Article 4

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (5) The costs of translation into languages of minorities in the Republic of Croatia incurred by the application of the provisions of the Constitution and the Act on the Right of Minorities in the Republic of Croatia to Use Their Language as well as the costs of interpretation and translation for the benefit of the defendant within the meaning of Article 202, paragraph 3, of this Act shall not be borne by persons who under the provisions of this Act are required to reimburse the costs of criminal proceedings.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Quality of the interpretation and translation

items.text: 1. Member States shall take concrete measures to ensure that the interpretation and translation provided meets the quality required under Article 2(8) and Article 3(9).

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (13(1))

nationalActs.titleEn: Judiciary Act

provisions.textEn: At the request of a court, state body, legal entity or citizen, permanent court interpreters translate spoken or written text from Croatian into a foreign language, from a foreign language into Croatian or from a foreign language into another foreign language.

(1) A person who has completed a graduate university degree, is fluent in an appropriate foreign language and a language in official use and has a satisfactory level of general and legal knowledge may be appointed as a permanent court interpreter.

(2) Permanent court interpreters shall be appointed and dismissed by the president of the county court. Permanent court interpreters are appointed for a term of four years, after which they may be reappointed. Appointed permanent court interpreters may provide translation services throughout the Republic of Croatia.

(4) The Minister of Justice shall prescribe by an ordinance the conditions and procedure for the appointment of permanent court interpreters, their rights and duties, as well as the amount of remuneration and reimbursement of expenses for their work.

items.text: 2. In order to promote the adequacy of interpretation and translation and efficient access thereto, Member States shall endeavour to establish a register or registers of independent translators and interpreters who are appropriately qualified. Once established, such register or registers shall, where appropriate, be made available to legal counsel and relevant authorities.

(5) The county court shall keep a list of permanent court interpreters appointed for its area.

(6) The list of permanent court interpreters for all courts shall be published on the website of the Ministry of Justice.

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that interpreters and translators be required to observe confidentiality regarding interpretation and translation provided under this Directive.

provisions.textEn: (1) Judges, lay judges, court clerks and employees, permanent court interpreters, experts and appraisers shall keep for themselves everything they have learned about the parties and their rights, obligations and legal interests in the performance of judicial duties, ie in the performance of other duties, and keep secrecy of all information that was not the subject of public discussion during the court proceedings.
(1) The obligation to maintain secrecy shall continue even after the termination of work in court.

provisions.textEn: The permanent court interpreter is obliged to keep secret everything he has learned while performing the duties of a permanent court interpreter.

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to pay special attention to the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter so as to ensure efficient and effective communication.
items.heading: Article 6

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: The training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings is organized through the Judicial Academy. In the last five years no training program on the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter was organized.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that when a suspected or accused person has been subject to questioning or hearings by an investigative or judicial authority with the assistance of an interpreter pursuant to Article 2, when an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents has been provided in the presence of such an authority pursuant to Article 3(7), or when a person has waived the right to translation pursuant to Article 3(8), it will be noted that these events have occurred, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.

provisions.textEn:
(1) The protocol shall contain the name of the government authority before which an action is taken, the location at which the said action is taken, the date and exact time when the action in question commences and ends, the names of the persons present, including in what capacity they are present, and the identification marking of the criminal case in which the action is taken. 

(2) The protocol must contain essential information on the course and contents of the action taken. Only the essential contents of statements and declarations made shall be entered in the protocol in the narrative form. Questions shall be recorded in the protocol only where this is necessary for understanding the answers. Where necessary, the question asked and the answer given to it shall be entered in the protocol verbatim. If objects and documents are seized in the course of taking an action, this shall be recorded in the protocol and the seized objects shall either be attached to the protocol or their location shall be stated. 

(3) When taking actions such as inspection, search, temporary seizure of objects or identification, information that is important in view of the significance of such an action or for determining the identity of certain objects (description, measures and size of objects or traces, marking of objects, etc.) shall also be entered in the protocol. Where sketches, drawings, blueprints, photographs, film or other technical recordings are made, this shall also be stated in the protocol and attached to it. 

(4) Special provisions on the protocol shall apply to the trial protocol (Articles 409 through 412), deliberation and voting protocols (Article 88) and other protocols as prescribed by this Act.

(1) The introduction of the protocol shall state the name of the court before which the trial takes place, the date, time and place of the session, the full name of the president of the panel, members of the panel, recorder, the prosecutors present, the accused and his defence counsel, the injured person and his statutory representative or proxy, interpreter, criminal offence under consideration and whether the trial is open or closed to the public.

provisions.textEn: (3) The parties to and other participants in the proceedings shall be entitled to use their native language, including the sign language of the deaf and the deaf and blind. If an act within the proceedings is not being taken in the language which the person speaks and understands, oral translation or sign language translation and interpretation for the deaf and the deaf and blind of what this person or another person is saying and of the documents and any other written evidentiary material being adduced shall be provided. It shall be noted in the minutes that the notification was read and statements by the participants given.
